writeup: TIC 365764494 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.560595 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.78 percent, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal registers a detection significance of 1042.2 on the automated pipeline's metric, and pixel-level analysis yields a peak signal-to-noise of 26.9, though with a centroid offset of 2.2 arcseconds from the target location. The candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs. An important open question remains: the pipeline's data quality metrics show that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, which suggests the true orbital period may be twice what an initial automated search indicated - the reported period of 1.560595 days accounts for this effect.
